codeReview.summary: Fail with one blocking issue. The feature adds first-class `flux apps generate-spec`, `verify-registration`, `verify-update`, `calculate-price`, `plan-registration`, `plan-update`, and `plan-renew` flows, persists reusable artifact resources, and surfaces registration/update/renew planning metadata in JSON. However, `apps generate-spec` parses `--cpu` as an integer >=1, which rejects valid Flux app-spec CPU values such as `0.5`; that means the CLI does not fully preserve v8 spec-generation behavior required by VAL-APPS-007.

issues.description: `parseAppsGenerateSpecArgs` registers `--cpu` as an integer flag with `min: 1`, so values like `--cpu 0.5` fail before the command reaches MCP (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:2472-2478`, `readIntegerFlagValue` at `fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:1941-1944`). Flux v8 app specs explicitly allow CPU in 0.1 increments (`codex/flux-cloud/references/app-spec-v8.md:116`), and the MCP-side generator already accepts fractional CPU values (`flux-mcp/src/index.ts:879-880`). This makes `flux apps generate-spec` reject valid spec-generation inputs and leaves VAL-APPS-007 incompletely implemented.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The mission shared library used by CLI workers does not capture app-spec resource constraints, so important rules such as fractional CPU support are easy to miss when implementing spec-generation parsers.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: The worker-read shared-state docs under `.factory/library/` (`architecture.md`, `shared-runtime.md`, etc.) do not mention v8 resource constraints, while `codex/flux-cloud/references/app-spec-v8.md:116` documents that CPU values may use 0.1 increments. The reviewed bug in `fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:2476` aligns with that missing shared knowledge.
